I've opened **[PR #397](https://github.com/cv/pit/pull/397)**. It says `Refs #396`, not `Closes`, and all 5 CI checks pass. It isn't merged or released yet, so the acceptance on a live pi-action thread is still to do; the PR lists those steps as a checklist.

## What changed
- **When it runs:** after every run that answers, including one that ended on a `terminate` round. The collapse goes into the same single `pit.context-edit` entry as the edits the model staged. The model's edits are recorded as before and the automatic ones as `operation: "collapse"`. A failed or aborted run collapses nothing and drops its staged edits, as before.
- **The line** looks like this:
  `[Pit: collapsed typescript call · "<label>" · workspace.read, workspace.search · ok · ~18.2K tokens · originals: session.inspectEntry("212"), session.inspectEntry("213")]`
  - The outcome is one of `ok`, `failed: <error's first line>`, `asked: <title>`, `saved <name>` or `no result`.
  - Other tools show their name and outcome.
  - An entry with several calls lists each one, separated by `;`.
- **What changes in the entry:** it keeps its text and thinking, signatures included. Its calls become the line and its results are omitted.
- **What it never touches:** user and host messages, answers, compaction summaries, notes, entries already rewritten or with a staged edit, entries no larger than their line, and the current run. If the model staged its own elide or summarize, the collapse skips those entries.
- **Compaction and forks:** it only reads the active context, so it never crosses the newest compaction head, and a fork keeps the view it had when it was taken.
- **Outline:** `session.outline()` shows collapsed entries as `elided`, with the line as the preview. I didn't add a new `collapsed` state, because the state type is part of the global contract shared with Pi.
- **Byte bound:** 512 bytes per line.
  - Labels and outcomes are cut to 160 characters each.
  - If the line is still too long, the injected functions go first, then the end of the description.

ops:
- The token size and the `inspectEntry` IDs are never cut. When they don't fit, the IDs switch to a shorter form.
  - One exception: if an entry has so many parallel calls that its IDs alone pass 512 bytes, the line keeps all the IDs and names no calls.
- **Guideline:** when
